key_findings.1_the_signal_is_real_and_linear: The agents->chat switch is LINEAR in the retained message count: 17ms@9, 27ms@168, 41ms@795(compacted), 272ms@7,390, ~2,500ms@~101k (0.0245ms/message). Kevin's ~500ms feel = the ~20k-message class. The <150ms pole is met only below ~5k messages. The reverse switch (chat->agents) is flat ~10.6ms at every class (the #2893/#2916 cuts holding), 26ms at the 101k class (the tip's teardown flush).
key_findings.2_the_dominant_term_is_the_full_ship: At the 7,390-message class the leg = wire+daemon-serialize+client-parse ~93ms + the visible-window first paint ~115ms + the extra round-trips ~30ms + the entries fold 8ms + the frames ~27ms. At 101k the full retained window ships: the wire+parse dominates (~2.4s of 2.5s). THE FULL-SHIP IS TS-PARITY-BOUND: TS's switch (openAgentsViewSession -> fresh DaemonAgentConnection.attach + getInitialSnapshot/get_messages) ships the same full retained window on every switch.
key_findings.3_the_core_cap_null_on-the-switch: The TS-parity newest-400 render window (attach-paint's cut) does NOT cut the switch leg at any class (the entries fold it cuts is 8ms@7,390 / ~110ms@101k of legs dominated by the wire): tip 263.9 vs core 275.1 (canon), 2497.2 vs 2526.3 (chained) — within noise. Its wins are the OPEN path (the sibling's legs) + the reverse-switch teardown at the big class (26.4 -> 10.5ms at 101k).
key_findings.4_served_path_proof_on_the_switch: The cap SERVES on the switch re-entry exactly per TS: the notice 'Showing latest 400 of 795 messages for faster open.' (large-real) and 'Showing latest 269 of 7,390 messages for faster open.' (canon/synth-70mib) found in the core arm's post-switch frames, absent in the tip arm; under-limit classes (small/medium) show no notice and identical leg timings.
key_findings.5_the_honest_floor_and_followups: The parity-bound floor for the switch at the big classes is the full-ship pipeline. The named follow-up cuts with measured bounds: (a) the resume-cursor incremental snapshot (the attach command already carries resume_cursor; shipping only the delta since the last attach cuts the wire to O(delta) — a PROTOCOL change beyond TS parity, needs its own lane + the operator's blessing; ~2.4s -> O(ms) at 101k), (b) the cross-switch visible-window layout reuse (the first pack re-renders the same visible entries on every switch; ~115ms -> ~0 on repeats; the repeat legs measured flat 272-310ms confirming the cache dies with the view), (c) the refresh_stats round-trip defer (~20ms; TS does not block its first frame on it).

honest_negative: The switch's cost at the big classes is STRUCTURAL at the TS-parity level (the full retained window ships per switch in both implementations); the cap restores the TS render shape (the sibling's cut) but the wire remains the floor. The decomposition record with the bounds stands as this lane's deliverable; no separate switch-path code fix is warranted by the decomposition (the fold is 8ms of 272ms at canon).
parity_notes: The TUI output bytes: the under-limit switch legs are unchanged by the cap (identical visible tails; the residual frame diffs are the A/A-class event/paint-phase non-determinism — roster rows, goal panels, bash-poll cards, the trial-name artifact — plus the frame-boundary phase); the capped classes differ exactly by the notice row + the un-rendered older rows (the served-path proof). Editor history/wire stay full-set per TS. TS-parity case: TS renders only the newest 400 at open/rebuild (INITIAL_TRANSCRIPT_RENDER_MESSAGE_LIMIT=400) — attach-paint's cut restores it; the port's switch inherits it via the shared reconstruct seam (verified: no separate switch call site needed).
outcome: MEASURED + DECOMPOSED + the stacked-core verified on the switch path (served-path + ABBA + the byte-class evidence). Kevin's signal confirmed real and attributed: linear in the retained message count, dominated by the TS-parity-bound full-ship wire+parse at the big classes; the pole met only under ~5k messages.
